r4.title: FEES NatSpec overstates the claim lock: with a challenge window longer than FEE_RAISE_DELAY, a fee cut made during the window can be reversed, with notice, before the heir is able to finalize
r4.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:94-98 (FEES header: "So the lock is a maximum: a cut during the challenge window still reaches the heir, whether it lowers the rate or removes the recipient."), and :1291-1292 (finalizeClaim: "lets a fee CUT made during the challenge window still reach the heir, while a rise cannot")
r4.problem: finalizeClaim charges min(lockedFeeBps, claimFeeBps()) at settlement, and nothing only if no recipient is in force AT SETTLEMENT. So a cut reaches the heir only if it is still in force when finalizeClaim is mined. The heir cannot finalize before finalizableAt = claimInitiatedAt + challengeWindow, and challengeWindow may be up to 365 days, while a raise (or switching the recipient back on) needs only FEE_RAISE_DELAY = 30 days. For any window of 30 days or more, the admin can cut on day 1 and schedule the old rate (or re-set the recipient) on day 2. Both take effect before the heir is able to settle, so the heir pays the full locked rate. The cut did not reach the heir, and the later rise did, back up to the lock. This is not a same-block sandwich (the notice is public), and the heir never pays more than they locked. But the text tells an heir who sees a cut that nothing more is needed. The only way to capture the cut is beneficiaryCancelClaim followed by initiateClaim while the cut is in force, which re-locks it at the price of a new full window. No earlier round tested a window longer than FEE_RAISE_DELAY: every F05/F06 test uses WINDOW = 14 days, where an heir who finalizes promptly does always capture the cut. It is the claim-lock analogue of F07's ceiling wording.
r4.evidence: Sandbox C:/Users/Vinoth/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Vinoth-OneDrive-Claude-claude-code/005aaa32-3c49-4f96-8428-bacda0a96f78/scratchpad/poc/REV4-closure-fresh/test/poc-REV4.ts (mocks in contracts/test/Rev4Mocks.sol), `npx hardhat test test/poc-REV4.ts`, 8 passing on the unmodified v2 contract. (1) "FEES NatSpec: with a challenge window longer than FEE_RAISE_DELAY...": a 60-day window with 50 bps locked. setClaimFee(0) on day 1; finalizeClaim reverts ChallengeWindowOpen while the cut is in force. setClaimFee(50) on day 2 is scheduled for day 32. At finalizableAt, ClaimSettled(alice, 0, bob, 99.5 ETH, 0.5 ETH): the full locked fee. (2) The same with setFeeRecipient(0) on day 1 and setFeeRecipient(feeSink) on day 2 (feeRecipientActiveAt = day 32): fee 0.5 ETH. (3) (control) cancel + re-initiate while the cut is in force settles with fee 0, after a fresh 60-day window. (4) The test asserts both quoted sentences are present in the source.
r4.fix: Reword both places. Suggested text: "a cut still in force when finalizeClaim is mined reaches the heir; a cut reversed before then (a raise or a recipient switch-on, each with FEE_RAISE_DELAY notice) does not, and with a challenge window longer than FEE_RAISE_DELAY that can happen before the heir is able to settle. An heir captures a cut for good only by beneficiaryCancelClaim + initiateClaim while it is in force, which restarts the window." In finalizeClaim, say "while a rise can never take it above the lock". APP (v2): show heirs any pending raise or recipient switch-on whose effective time falls before finalizableAt. Optional code change that makes the original promise true: a permissionless ratchetLockedFee(vaultOwner, vaultId). While CLAIM_PENDING, it sets lockedFeeBps = min(lockedFeeBps, the fee in force now, which is 0 when no recipient is in force). It can only lower the lock, restarts nothing, and costs a few dozen bytes.

r4.title: F09 class gap: a same-chain ledger that credits msg.sender on receive (the canonical ERC-4337 EntryPoints on Base and BNB) passes both the address rule and the payout measurement, stranding the payout as a vault-owned deposit nobody can withdraw
r4.problem: Review round 2 refused the OP-stack predeploy range because the L2ToL1MessagePasser credits msg.sender (the vault) on receive. The NatSpec says no rule can see a payee that forwards to this contract's address on ANOTHER chain. It does not cover the same-chain version: a contract whose receive() books the value to msg.sender in its own ledger. The ERC-4337 EntryPoints v0.6 (0x5FF137D4b0FDCD49DcA30c7CF57E578a026d2789), v0.7 (0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032) and v0.8 (0x4337084D9E255Ff0702461CF8895CE9E3b5Ff108) are deployed at the same addresses on both target chains, and receive() calls depositTo(msg.sender). A native withdrawCredit, pushCredit (by anyone after PUSH_GRACE) or claim payout to one of them passes _checkPayee. It also passes the _holdings measurement: the native balance falls by exactly `amount`, and no listed token moves. The payout becomes an EntryPoint deposit owned by the vault, and only the vault can withdraw it, with withdrawTo, a call it has no function to make. So it is stranded for good. It is not surplus, so T4 (no admin reach) still holds. This is a user-error loss of the same shape as the passer, which was fixed as an informational item, but less plausible because nobody types an EntryPoint to mean "withdraw to L1". Other contracts in this class (e.g. staking or deposit contracts whose receive() mints to the sender) behave the same way.

r4.title: The round-3 F01 source guard accepts a parenthesised delete of the list
r4.location: test/AuditPrelim2026-09.ts:340-361 (the read whitelist; the prefix check `/(?:\bdelete|\+\+|--)$/` at :360)
r4.problem: Round 3 rewrote the guard so that every mention of isSupportedToken or _supportedTokens outside the constructor must be a known read form: an indexed read 'not preceded by delete'. The check looks only at the text right before the identifier. In `delete (_supportedTokens[i])` or `delete(isSupportedToken[t])` that text ends in '(', so it does not match. The indexed mention is then classed as a read, and the function-name layer passes any innocuous name. The array form is the harmful one. Blanking WETH's slot in _supportedTokens makes _holdings read address(0), which counts as a failed read on both sides, so WETH stops being measured. isSupportedToken[weth] stays true, so sweepSurplus(weth) still works. That reopens the F09 wrap-and-return sweep of an heir's native payout, the regression this guard exists to catch.
r4.evidence: A mutant inserts `function tidy(uint256 i) external onlyOwner { delete (_supportedTokens[i]); }` (GB), the same without the space (GB2), and `function tidy(address t) external onlyOwner { delete (isSupportedToken[t]); }` (GA). Each compiles and the vault suite gives 224 passing, 0 failing, including '(guard) the list is written only in the constructor: outside it the source only reads the list, in known read forms'. See C:/Users/Vinoth/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Vinoth-OneDrive-Claude-claude-code/005aaa32-3c49-4f96-8428-bacda0a96f78/scratchpad/poc/R4-tests-guard/guard-console.txt and guard-mut-GA/GB/GB2.log. The runner is mutate-guard.js.
r4.fix: Look through parentheses before the identifier: strip `(` and whitespace from the prefix before testing for delete, ++ or --. Or refuse any `delete` whose operand mentions either name. A more robust option walks the solc AST (Assignment, UnaryOperation delete/++/--, MemberAccess push/pop, and any storage-typed VariableDeclaration or argument) for references to the two declarations.

r5.title: A payee that books value to msg.sender but lets anyone release it to the owner makes a mis-routed payout sweepable; PAYOUT ADDRESSES and the round-4 pin say it never is
r5.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:141-153 (PAYOUT ADDRESSES: "the payout is lost, though never sweepable" ... "no rule can see either kind in general: ... one that books the value to msg.sender in a ledger of its own"); test/AuditPrelim2026-09.ts:724 and :745 (the pin says "a claim it can never exercise, and nothing is sweepable" and asserts that sentence)
r5.problem: Round 4 describes the whole class of ledgers that book value to msg.sender as "lost, though never sweepable". That holds only when the booking can be withdrawn by its owner and nobody else, as with an EntryPoint. Some ledgers let anyone release a booking to its owner and fall back to WETH when the owner refuses native coin (the common "ETH, else WETH" refund used by Nouns, Zora and Foundation). Others force-send native coin, for example with SELFDESTRUCT or Solady's forceSafeTransferETH. With either kind, the value comes back to the vault. The vault's receive() revert is exactly what triggers the WETH fallback. The returned value lands outside every lane as a listed token or native coin, so it is surplus, and the admin can trigger the release and then sweep it. The lane arithmetic in T4 still holds: the credit was really paid out, and the separate "(Value a payee sends back later ... was paid)" sentence covers this case. The heir loses the value either way, because they named the wrong recipient. What changes is who ends up with it: the admin can capture it, while the NatSpec and the pin tell auditors and app authors that nobody can.

Sandbox C:/Users/Vinoth/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Vinoth-OneDrive-Claude-claude-code/005aaa32-3c49-4f96-8428-bacda0a96f78/scratchpad/poc/R5SEC. A ledger that lets anyone release a booking to its owner, in a listed token or by force-sending native coin, returns it here as surplus, which sweepSurplus can take (as "Value a payee sends back later ... was paid" already implies).

r5.title: F20 x F13: the heir's typo remedy stops working at finalizableAt, because anyone's finalizeClaim can land first
r5.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:1239-1282 (beneficiaryCancelClaim and its NatSpec), 1302-1309 (finalizeClaim is permissionless from finalizableAt)
r5.problem: F20 added beneficiaryCancelClaim so an heir can fix a mistyped payout address. The NatSpec says the undo is available "until finalizeClaim is mined". But finalizeClaim is permissionless from finalizableAt, and the header tells anyone to call it. So in practice the fix only guarantees a correction during the challenge window. Suppose the heir notices the typo at or after finalizableAt. A keeper that finalizes everything finalizable, or a griefer, can be mined first. The estate is then credited to the mistyped address for good: only that address can withdraw it, and a push after PUSH_GRACE can only deliver it there. That is F20's original loss, cut down to a window of at least 7 days but not removed, and nothing tells the heir where the deadline is. No previous round tested this race: they tried the stolen-key redirect (round 1), the ACTIVE gap (round 2) and the fee re-lock (round 4).
r5.evidence: Sandbox scratchpad/poc/REV5-closure/test/poc-REV5.ts, test "F20 x F13: the heir's typo remedy ends in practice at finalizableAt ..." (passing: it asserts the defect). Setup: bob initiates with recipient 0x...dEaD, WINDOW 7 days. At block time == finalizableAt, one block holds [carol finalizeClaim (tip 100 gwei), bob beneficiaryCancelClaim (tip 2 gwei)]. Statuses are [1, 0] (the cancel reverts NoClaimPending). creditOf(NATIVE, 0x...dEaD) == 99.5 ETH. bob's withdrawCredit reverts NothingCredited. After PUSH_GRACE, carol's pushCredit moves 99.5 ETH into 0x...dEaD (changeEtherBalance). Control in the same file: the same pair at finalizableAt - 1 gives [0, 1], and the re-initiated claim settles 99.5 ETH to bob. The sandbox baseline, the vault suite with no changes, gives 231 passing, the same count as round 4.
r5.fix: NatSpec, DOC and APP (v2): say that the last safe moment to correct the recipient is finalizableAt, not "until finalizeClaim is mined". The app should confirm the recipient at initiateClaim (as F20's APP part already plans) and show a countdown to finalizableAt as the deadline for any correction. Optional code change (lead decision): for a short grace after finalizableAt (for example 72 h), let only the beneficiary or claimRecipient call finalizeClaim, and let anyone call it after that. The beneficiary already needed its key to initiate, so this costs honest heirs nothing, and settlement stays permissionless after the grace.

r5.title: F09 (round-4 extension): Venus vBNB on BNB Chain credits msg.sender on a plain transfer, the same shape as the EntryPoints, but is not refused
r5.problem: Round 4 refused the four EntryPoints by address. Its reason was that a plain native transfer to them always books the value to msg.sender, so no legitimate payout goes there, and the refusal costs a few comparisons. The same reasoning applies to Venus vBNB (0xA07c5b74C9B40447a954e1466938b865b6BBea36), a large Compound-style CEther market on one of the two target chains: its fallback mints vBNB to msg.sender. Suppose an heir names vBNB as the claim recipient or withdrawCredit `to`, for example to "deposit into Venus". Then the credit is retired and the vault ends up holding vBNB. The vault has no call that can redeem it, and sweepSurplus refuses it because it is unlisted. T4 holds (nothing is sweepable), but the heir loses the whole payout. It belongs to the residual class the NatSpec already discloses ("a staking or deposit contract that credits its sender"). This is its most prominent instance on the target chains, and the round-4 standard would refuse it.
r5.evidence: Read-only RPC on bsc-dataseed.binance.org. eth_getCode(vBNB) is 19,905 bytes on BNB; the same address has no code on mainnet.base.org. eth_call {from: WBNB contract, to: vBNB, value: 0.001 BNB, data: 0x} returns success (0x). eth_simulateV1 from 0x1111...1111 (balance overridden) sends 0.001 BNB to vBNB: status 1, and a Mint event (topic 0x4c209b5f) names the sender as minter. A following balanceOf(sender) returns 4,008,588 vBNB units. Saved in scratchpad/poc/REV5-closure/vbnb-simulate.json. For comparison: EntryPoints v0.4 and v0.5 have no code on either chain, and BNB system contracts 0x...1002 and 0x...1004 keep the value (receiveDeposit) rather than crediting the sender.
r5.fix: Add 0xA07c5b74C9B40447a954e1466938b865b6BBea36 to _checkPayee as a constant. It is free on Base, where the address is empty. Name it in PAYOUT ADDRESSES as a refused instance of the credit-the-sender class. Whether or not the contract changes, add it to the BNB app's refused payout, withdraw and claim-recipient list, next to the EntryPoints and the OP-stack range.

r5.title: Round 3's reordered terminal-state test in checkIn has no test for its SETTLED case, and neither does checkInMany's SKIP_TERMINAL
r5.location: contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:916 (checkIn `if (s != STATE_ACTIVE && s != STATE_CLAIM_PENDING) revert VaultNotActive`), :971 (checkInMany `else if (s != STATE_ACTIVE) skip = SKIP_TERMINAL`); tests only use CLOSED: test/AuditPrelim2026-09.ts:3454-3460 and :3533, test/InheritanceVault.ts:370, AuditPrelim:3338
r5.problem: Round 3 replaced checkIn's `s != STATE_ACTIVE` with the compound `s != STATE_ACTIVE && s != STATE_CLAIM_PENDING`. CHANGELOG round 3 item 3 says "A settled or closed vault still reverts VaultNotActive", but every terminal-vault assertion in the suite uses a CLOSED vault. No test calls checkIn or checkInMany on a SETTLED vault. So a regression that drops SETTLED from either terminal test goes unnoticed. Under that regression, checkIn on a settled estate succeeds and logs CheckedIn (a green toast after the heir has already been paid). checkInMany would count the settled vault as refreshed, so a one-vault keeper never gets NothingCheckedIn. No value moves: a settled vault holds 0. The closest earlier item is round 4 item 7 (H3, the same function, Informational).
r5.evidence: Sandbox scratchpad/poc/R5-tests-mut2, mutate-r5b.js. H9: checkIn `if (s == STATE_CLOSED) revert VaultNotActive(...)`. K8: checkInMany `else if (s == STATE_CLOSED) skip = SKIP_TERMINAL`. Each gives 231 passing, 0 failing on the vault suite, AuditPrelim + Audit + InheritanceVault (r5b-mutants-result.txt, mut-H9.txt, mut-K8.txt). The full suite adds only NotifySubscription.ts, which never touches the vault. Failing test: scratchpad/poc/R5-tests/test/poc-R5-tests.ts "SETTLED is terminal for checkIn and checkInMany, before and past its horizon". It passes on the current source (3 passing). Against the mutants (r5b-poc-result.txt): under H9, "Expected transaction to be reverted with custom error 'VaultNotActive', but it didn't revert"; under K8, "expected [ '0:in', '2:in' ] to deeply equal [ '0:skip2', '2:in' ]".
r5.fix: Extend the F15 round-3 test's terminal-vault control (or add the PoC test). Settle one vault with its horizon far off and one whose horizon then passes. Assert checkIn gives VaultNotActive(id, 3) both before and past the horizon (never HorizonReached). Assert checkInMany([settled, healthy]) logs `settled:skip2`, and checkInMany([settled]) reverts NothingCheckedIn(4).

r5.title: The F27 guard "the deadline is written in exactly one place" is still a text regex; delete, tuple assignment and ++ writes survive the whole suite
r5.location: test/AuditPrelim2026-09.ts:3676-3694 (regex `/\.deadline\s*(?:[-+*\/%|&^]|<<|>>)?=(?!=)/`); protects contracts/InheritanceVault.sol:619-623 (_resetClock, the only writer that emits DeadlineReset)
r5.problem: Round 4 moved the F01 and ACCOUNTING guards to the compiler AST. Its own reason was that text guards "can always be dodged by a spelling the pattern did not foresee". The F27 deadline-write guard was not moved and has the same holes. `delete v.deadline`, `(v.deadline, x) = (...)` and `v.deadline++` never match its regex. The behavioural F27 test covers only the owner actions it lists, not initiateClaim, beneficiaryCancelClaim or finalizeClaim. So a deadline write with no DeadlineReset in those paths passes everything. That breaks F27's promise that DeadlineReset is a complete record for an events-only indexer. The harmful case, a topUp that resets the clock, is still caught behaviourally (InheritanceVault.ts:196), so there is no fund impact.
r5.evidence: Sandbox scratchpad/poc/R5-tests-mut2. Three mutants each give 231 passing, 0 failing (mut-F27a.txt, mut-F27b.txt, mut-F27c.txt): F27a adds `delete v.deadline;` in finalizeClaim; F27b makes initiateClaim write `(v.deadline, v.claimRecipient) = (uint64(block.timestamp), recipient);`; F27c adds `v.deadline++;` in initiateClaim. Two tests in scratchpad/poc/R5-tests/test/poc-R5-tests.ts pass on the current source and fail on all three (r5b-poc-result.txt): "DeadlineReset is a complete record ... through a claim, a cancel and a settlement" and the AST guard. The AST guard reports, for example, "expected [ '_resetClock', 'initiateClaim' ] to deeply equal [ '_resetClock' ]" under F27b.
r5.fix: Add an AST layer, as round 4 did for F01. Every MemberAccess `deadline` with lValueRequested == true whose expression type is `struct InheritanceVault.Vault storage...` must sit in _resetClock. Anchor the type match with `storage`, because getVault's `o.deadline` is a VaultView memory write. Optionally add the behavioural check that storage equals the last indexed DeadlineReset after initiateClaim, beneficiaryCancelClaim and finalizeClaim. Both are in poc-R5-tests.ts.
